purpose: Restore selected GEECon compositions with corrected factual content, after user review.

prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit / infographic-diagram.
Edit target: supplied GEECon full kill chain illustration. This is an update of a liked existing diagram, not a redesign into cards. Keep its wide 16:9 composition, dark near-black background, fine cyan connectors, violet numbered hexagons, small platform/file/tool icons and dense interconnected developer / CI / cloud / registry / GitHub network. Keep the main map on the left four fifths and six-stage legend at the far right. Preserve the source illustration's authored character and readable typography.

Correct the content:
- Top npm registry distributes a poisoned package to a developer workstation or CI/CD runner.
- Stage 1 is a preinstall loader. Stage 2 searches environment, local files and cloud credentials with TruffleHog.
- Usable npm publishing identity connects back to the registry: poison more releases, then the next install repeats the loop.
- Usable GitHub identity permits public-repository exfiltration and, separately, malicious workflow / self-hosted runner access. Public repositories are dead drops, not packages.
- Represent these as available-identity branches, not a single yes/no test where any failure causes deletion.
- A separate red destructive-fallback branch is conditioned explicitly on BOTH: no GitHub token available AND no valid npm token. The branch must not imply that any blocked exfiltration wipes everything.
- Persistent runner / workflow access is a reported capability, not a claim of operator command use on every host.

Remove the entire bottom statistics strip (843 / 33K / 25K / 1195) and all quantitative impact assertions everywhere. Replace that lower strip with a quiet dark area, no text or logos. Do not put victim totals into the diagram.
Use concise labels. Exact six-stage legend:
1 Preinstall execution
2 Credential discovery
3 Token-enabled propagation
4 Public-repository exfiltration
5 Workflow / runner backdoor
6 Destructive fallback
Below stage 6 in smaller type: "No GitHub token AND no valid npm token".
Keep the complete network and its feedback loops, rather than simplifying into six disconnected boxes. No title in the image; the slide adds it. Fix typos such as "packagers". No new decorative cyber elements or corporate branding.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied full kill chain diagram. Preserve absolutely all layout, text, legend, colors, numbered stages and icon placements. Correct only three connector-direction mistakes:
1. Between the center "Exposed tokens and secrets" node and the box ABOVE it labeled "Publish more poisoned releases", the vertical arrow must point UP from exposed credentials to publishing. Remove the downward arrow pointing into the secrets node. The nearby "npm publish token" label describes this upward path. From publishing, arrows continue UP into Other packages in the npm registry.
2. The red destructive-fallback path must flow OUT from the right side of "Exposed tokens and secrets", rightward then DOWN into "No GitHub token AND no valid npm token", then DOWN into "Destructive fallback". Remove the red arrowhead that currently points LEFT into the secrets node. Put the arrowhead at entry to the condition box instead.
3. The connection labeled "GitHub token" must be a single arrow pointing RIGHT from "Exposed tokens and secrets" INTO "GitHub access". Remove the left-pointing return arrow and any redundant unlabeled parallel line between those two nodes.
Do not change any other content or geometry. Do not add any text, statistics or title. This is exact directional correction of a technical diagram.

Use case: precise-object-edit. This technical diagram is almost final. Preserve its style, exact layout and all six legend items. Make only these final cleanup changes for unambiguous flow:
- Delete the redundant upper middle node "Publish new malicious release" (and its stage 3 hexagon), the "Valid npm token" label, and the entire cyan connector from the right side of Exposed tokens and secrets up through those two elements into the RIGHT edge of the npm registry. Fill their space with the matching dark background. The ONE remaining npm propagation route is the already-correct UP arrow from Exposed tokens and secrets through "npm publish token" to "Publish more poisoned releases" and up into Other packages. Put the violet stage 3 hexagon immediately to the LEFT of that remaining publishing box.
- Remove the return cyan connector from "Push to public repo (dead drop)" down its right side back LEFT into GitHub access. Retain the other path from GitHub access UP to the dead-drop box and from there UP/RIGHT into the public repositories. Exfiltration flows outward.
- Inside Developer machine / CI/CD runner, remove the horizontal arrow between the two Install poisoned package boxes. They are alternative execution environments. Draw a short DOWN connector from EACH install box into the shared "Search env, local files and cloud creds (TruffleHog)" box.
Everything else must remain unchanged, especially the red condition and fallback, single GitHub-token arrow, stage labels and dark bottom without statistics. Do not introduce new labels, connections or objects.
assets.notes: Full-map composition retained. Impact totals removed, destructive-fallback condition corrected, alternative install paths and credential propagation arrows repaired. This is a conceptual capability map, not a captured execution trace.

prompts:

Edit target: supplied GEECon "pattern is clear" artwork. Keep its wide 16:9 composition, dark uncluttered left 45 percent for slide text, and distinctive right-side visual of package, workflow, code, extension and workstation inputs feeding an AI amplifier which reaches many connected identities and tools. Preserve the colors, precise rendering, perspective and dramatic restrained light. This is a faithful factual cleanup of an existing liked slide background.
Remove the entire bottom chart that labels 2025 and 2026 and depicts an exponential growth curve. It is unsupported quantitative evidence. Replace that area with the physical dark desktop / subdued console continuing naturally from the surrounding scene, without any graph, axis, years, numbers or labels. Remove the tiny bar/line charts and world-map metrics in the background too; leave subdued dark panels without measured data. Keep the central conceptual amplification network on the right. The concept is more possible input and tool reach, not a measured attack growth rate. Keep the left text space completely clean. No new text, no watermark.
assets.notes: Conceptual AI amplifier preserved. Unsupported growth chart, years and measured-looking dashboard graphs removed. Actual counts are editable slide text with a documented sample method.
Copied unchanged. Incident labels, dates and factual claims are editable slide content with source links in speaker notes.
